question: If x + 1/x = 11, then x² + 1/x² is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an **algebraic expression** of the form **x + 1/x = k**, the value of **x² + 1/x²** is given by the formula **k² − 2**.

Given: **x + 1/x = 11**, so **k = 11**.

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 11² − 2**

⇒ **121 − 2 = 119**

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **x + 1/x = 11**

To find the value of **x² + 1/x²**, we use the **square identity**:

Formula: **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab**

⇒ **(x + 1/x)² = (11)²**

⇒ **x² + (1/x)² + 2 × x × (1/x) = 121**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² + 2 = 121**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 121 − 2**

⇒ **x² + 1/x² = 119**

**∴ The correct answer is 119.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Sign Identity

If **x − 1/x = k**, then **x² + 1/x² = k² + 2**.

Cubic Identity

If **x + 1/x = k**, then **x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k**.

Higher Power (Fourth)

To find **x⁴ + 1/x⁴**, square the value of **(x² + 1/x²)** and subtract 2.</p
